2_Introduction: A significantly higher JSC of 24.959 mA/cm² is obtained while preserving VOC of 1.1334 V and FF of 84.2207%, resulting in the highest PCE of 23.8246% at reverse scan. The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. CB (160 µL) was dropped at the center of the spinning substrate approximately 10 s before the end of the spin coating procedure. After the spin coating was completed, it was annealed on a hot stage at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation itself delivers critical structural and electronic advantages: the mixed A-site cation ensemble enhances Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.98), suppresses δ-phase formation, and mitigates halide vacancy-mediated ion migration, while the near-stoichiometric iodide content minimizes PbI₂ residuals that act as recombination centers; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration—optimized to balance viscosity and nucleation density—combined with the two-step spin-coating profile (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction) enables uniform nucleation across the substrate, and the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with chlorobenzene (160 µL delivered ~10 s before spin termination) arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution at the optimal metastable window, promoting oriented growth of large, low-angle-grain perovskite domains with suppressed grain boundary area; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete ligand ejection and lattice consolidation without inducing volatile loss or phase segregation, yielding films with high phase purity—as corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ XRD peaks near 12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—low non-radiative trap density—as evidenced by strong, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and long carrier lifetime in PL mapping—and exceptional morphological continuity—as confirmed by high film coverage metrics and uniform grayscale intensity in optical microscopy, collectively minimizing shunt pathways and interfacial recombination losses; this synergistic crystallization control and intrinsic compositional stability translate directly into balanced charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and robust fill factor, delivering VOC = 1.1334 V, JSC = 24.959 mA/cm², FF = 84.2207%, and PCE = 23.8246%.
